newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - high-grades firm, McLeods gain.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - high-grades firm, McLeods gain.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were firmly bid, but thinly traded on Monday, while high-yields resumed gains ahead of another brisk week of supply, dealers across both markets said.

High-yield secondary prices were firmer by 1/4 point, with exceptional gains for McLeodUSA Inc after the company announced its intention to merge with midwest telecommunication company Consolidated Communications Inc.
McLeodUSA's $500 million in zero coupon debt rose more than two points to a 64-1/2 bid, 65 offer in moderate activity, traders said.

Douglas Conn, vice president and high-yield analyst at Lehman Brothers, said McLeodUSA, which operates in the mountain and midwestern states, will benefit from Consolidated's telephone operations and fiber optic links between urban areas in the midwest.

"This (merger) allows McLeod to buy facilities to build out his super-regional network at a faster pace," Conn said, adding that chairman and chief executive Clark McLeod is also getting a cash-flow positive company with a long operating history.

Standard & Poor's affirmed its single-B rating on the debt, citing the complementary nature of the merger. But S&P also said it expects cash flow to remain weak over the next several years, precluding an upgrade.

In other high-yield news, Pathmark Stores debt rallied after the company reported gains in same store sales and steady operating cash flow, traders and analysts said. Cash flow for the first quarter fell to $48.3 million from $54.2 million one year earlier, Pathmark said, but analysts said the results were strong enough to assuage the Street's fears of a deeper decline.
Pathmark's zero coupon debt gained more than three points to 66-3/4 bid and its 9-5/8s of 2003 gained just over two points to 96-1/4.

New high-yield issues set for pricing late on Monday or Tuesday include $150 million 144A senior notes from Verio Inc at 13 percent to 13-1/4 percent with warrants; $115 million 144A senior notes from North Atlantic Trading Co at 11 percent to 11-1/4 percent; and $100 million 144A senior notes from Drypers Corp.

Turning to investment grades, secondary activity was next to nil but players were eagerly awaiting about $4.0 billion in new supply slated for the week. In addition, more issuers are expected to engineer speedy offerings to capitalize on the drop in interest rates that followed soft economic and inflation reports last week.

In fact, high-grade issuance hit a six-month record high of $178.6 billion during the first half of 1997, while straight corporate debt also hit a record of $192 billion, according to Securities Data Co.

Issuance on Monday featured $200 million 10-year senior notes from Norwest Corp priced as 6-3/4s to yield 46 basis points over Treasuries via UBS Securities and $100 million seven-year debt from FINOVA Capital Corp priced as 6.90s to yield 55 basis points over the curve via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

In U.S. Treasuries, bullish momentum pushed prices higher in a lackluster session despite talk of an overbought market, according to analysts there. The benchmark 30-year bond gained 13/32 to yield 6.70 percent and the 10-year T-note rose 8/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
